name: Mistral Small 3.1 24B Instruct
definition: Mistral Small 3.1 24B Instruct is a dense multimodal instruction model developed by Mistral AI in the Mistral Small 3.1 family. It has 24B parameters, supports 128K tokens of context, accepts Text + images and produces Text. Its primary role is general-purpose multimodal assistants, function calling, documents, coding and local inference.

key_topics: general-purpose multimodal assistants, function calling, documents, coding and local inference

details: Multimodal vision encoder inherited from the Pixtral-style Mistral stack

training.summary: Mistral Small 3.1 extends the Small family with native image understanding, multilingual instruction following and long context. It is tuned for practical assistant, coding, function-calling and document workflows while staying materially smaller than frontier-scale MoE systems.

license.name: Apache License 2.0
license.special_conditions: Includes an express patent grant. Model-specific acceptable-use policies, if separately published, are not automatically part of Apache 2.0.
license.legal_note: OpenWeightModels summary for technical comparison; not legal advice.

deployments.notes: Mistral notes that quantized deployments can fit a single RTX 4090 or 32GB-RAM MacBook.

hardware.summary: At 24B dense parameters, full precision is a serious workstation/server model but quantization can bring it into single-high-end-GPU or 32GB unified-memory territory. Vision and 128K context still increase runtime memory beyond weight storage alone.

limitations: Quantized “fits” statements do not guarantee 128K context at the same memory target.
Visual inputs add preprocessing and token overhead.
Function calling quality depends on schema/prompt/runtime integration.
Apache 2.0 simplifies licensing but application-level safety obligations remain.
